blogs.title: Breaking the 2 Million Token Barrier: How LongRoPE Unlocks Massive Context Windows
blogs.description: This post introduces the core achievement of LongRoPE: extending Large Language Model context windows from the typical 128k limit to an astonishing 2,048k tokens. We'll explore why previous attempts stalled at lower limits due to 'catastrophic forgetting' and data scarcity, and how this new method achieves a 512x expansion with minimal fine-tuning.

blogs.title: Beyond Linear Scaling: Why Non-Uniform Positional Embeddings Matter
blogs.description: Dive deep into the technical innovation behind LongRoPE. Most existing methods treat all parts of a sentence equally when stretching context, but this article explains the discovery that RoPE (Rotary Positional Embedding) has inherent 'non-uniformities.' Learn how exploiting these variations across different dimensions and token positions creates a smarter, more efficient way to stretch context without losing information.

blogs.title: The Progressive Strategy: Reaching Extreme Lengths Without Breaking Your Budget
blogs.description: Training on millions of tokens is incredibly expensive. This blog breaks down LongRoPE's clever 'progressive extension' strategy. Instead of trying to train a model from scratch on massive data, we'll walk through how researchers first extend to 256k with fine-tuning, then use an intelligent search algorithm to jump to 2 million tokens without needing another round of costly training.

blogs.title: Don't Lose Your Short-Term Memory: Recovering Performance at Small Context Sizes
blogs.description: A common pitfall in extending context windows is hurting performance on short inputs (like standard chat prompts). This post explains LongRoPE's unique solution for 'context recovery,' where the model dynamically adjusts its positional embeddings during inference to ensure it still excels at tasks requiring only 4k–8k tokens while being capable of handling millions.
